title: Experiment: read and `<Suspense>` confinement, four detectors falsified twice over
summary: A second static analysis was added: it scans every module under `app/`, asserts the designated reader exists and was examined, and emits four kinds of violation. Six fixtures, one per detected violation plus an allowed control: ALLOWED reported clean with a consumer present; DIRECT caught a component importing an adapter at line 1; INDIRECT caught a helper re-exporting the adapter at its own line 1, not at the page that used it; MISSING-BOUNDARY caught `<Panel>` rendered bare at the rendering site, line 3; FS-DIRECT caught `node:fs` at line 1; ROUTE-READ caught a route entry awaiting the reader at line 3. Each of the four detectors was then falsified again against a TEMPORARY violation inserted into the real application, and each reported the real file and line before being reverted. A missing reader is reported as `readerSeen: false` rather than as a clean project.

facts.analysis: static, text only; no application code executed

omissions.reason: No module in the real application consumes the reader yet — the lint reports `0 reader consumer(s)`. The two boundary detectors therefore have nothing to examine there and were falsified against temporary real-code violations and against fixtures instead. They begin covering real code at TSK-0007.

A component's enclosure is judged where it is RENDERED by name. A component passed as a prop, rendered through a variable, or wrapped by a boundary in a parent layout rather than at the call site would not be judged correctly. No such pattern exists yet; it is a real limit rather than a hypothetical one.
Unchanged from the import half: a computed specifier cannot be resolved by text, and the lint exits non-zero on one rather than passing over it.

notes: ⚠️ THE FIXTURES CAUGHT THREE DEFECTS, TWO OF THEM IN THE FIXTURES THEMSELVES. (1) The fixture components imported the reader with `../_read/planning` from `app/`, which climbs OUT of the app directory — so nothing resolved, `consumers` was empty, and the ALLOWED case reported clean for the worst possible reason. The `consumers.length > 0` assertion is what caught it, and it was written for exactly that. (2) A `sed` fix then broke the indirect fixture's path in the other direction. (3) In the analyser, two `new RegExp` template literals lost a backslash level, so `await\s+` became `awaits+` and matched nothing — a detector that silently could not fire. ⚠️ FIXTURES ARE `.jsx` BECAUSE `node --test` COLLECTS `.js` UNDER `test/`, and these contain JSX that Node cannot parse. Collected, they failed the suite for a reason unrelated to what they test. `.jsx` sits outside the runner's patterns and inside the analyser's.
